physical_mechanism: Kinetic penetration by a solid steel projectile; target may crater, plug, shear, bend, crack and spall
projectile_parts_to_model: projectile body and nose; cap only if that variant has one
material_models_needed: projectile and target plasticity, strain-rate dependence, damage/failure, contact/friction; projectile deformation may be significant
outputs: perforation/stoppage; residual velocity; projectile deformation/break-up; target plug/crater; back-face bulge/spall; ricochet/deflection
common_wrong_shortcut: one penetration number vs effective thickness
initial_support: Phase 1 general solver verification; history-specific ammo later

physical_mechanism: Kinetic AP body; hard/tough cap alters initial impact behaviour; ballistic wind cap is primarily aerodynamic and is not the same thing as the AP cap
projectile_parts_to_model: body, AP cap, ballistic cap, base cavity/fuze/filler where applicable; separate contacts/bonds/materials
material_models_needed: multi-material projectile, cap deformation/failure, rate-dependent armor plasticity and fracture, possible projectile break-up, oblique impact
outputs: same as AP plus projectile cap deformation and post-penetration HE effect if the round survives/functioning is modelled
common_wrong_shortcut: treat caps as decorative and use only projectile mass/speed
initial_support: first historical projectile family for Tiger I and Tiger II

physical_mechanism: AP penetration mechanics first; base fuze then initiates HE after functioning delay/arming conditions
projectile_parts_to_model: AP body, filler cavity, base fuze and delay/arming state
material_models_needed: AP model plus event sequencing and HE blast/fragmentation
outputs: perforation, residual projectile, time/distance to detonation, internal fragments/blast
common_wrong_shortcut: treat explosive filler as the penetrator or trigger it at first contact
initial_support: Pzgr.39 family, but HE subsystem can be staged after mechanical solver validates

physical_mechanism: Dense small-diameter core carries most penetrator work; lighter shell/body separates or deforms; often strong against some plate conditions but sensitive to target hardness and obliquity
projectile_parts_to_model: core, sheath/jacket, nose/cap and any tracer/fuze parts if present
material_models_needed: multi-material core/steel, core fracture/erosion, obliquity and target thickness effects
outputs: core residual velocity/deformation, jacket disruption, plate hole/plug, deflection/ricochet
common_wrong_shortcut: APCBC model + greater velocity or a static multiplier

physical_mechanism: Subcalibre penetrator with sabot discarded after muzzle; a penetrator of much smaller diameter interacts with the target
projectile_parts_to_model: penetrator only at target plus remaining sabot effects if near-target interaction matters
material_models_needed: core geometry/material and high-strain-rate target; stabilization/flight/dispersion is separate from terminal impact
outputs: penetrator erosion/deformation, residual velocity, ricochet and plate damage
common_wrong_shortcut: treat full-calibre projectile diameter as impact diameter

physical_mechanism: Long high-density rod penetrates through high-pressure plastic flow/erosion, with rod and target strengths/densities both important
projectile_parts_to_model: long rod, sabot/fin system for flight only, tail/base as needed
material_models_needed: rate-dependent strength, thermal softening/erosion, rod fracture/bending and high-speed contact; Alekseevskii–Tate-style models can guide lower-order models
outputs: penetration depth/time, rod erosion and residual length, target damage/spall
common_wrong_shortcut: reuse WWII short-shell parameters or fixed RHA penetration

physical_mechanism: Explosive charge collapses a liner to create a high-velocity metal jet that penetrates; outer projectile speed is not the primary penetration driver after charge formation, though functioning and impact conditions matter
projectile_parts_to_model: explosive charge, liner, casing, fuze, standoff geometry; jet is a time-evolving material flow
material_models_needed: detonation/liner collapse and jet penetration (or a validated reduced jet model), obliquity, stand-off and layered target interactions
outputs: jet penetration channel, jet breakup/consumption, spall and behind-armour effects
common_wrong_shortcut: represent as a solid shell with constant millimetres of penetration

physical_mechanism: Plastic explosive spreads on the surface; detonation shock induces tensile reflection and scabbing/spall on rear face; not conventional projectile perforation
material_models_needed: surface coupling, transient stress waves and tensile failure/spall; reduced-order model if full hydrocode unavailable
outputs: back-face scab fragments, internal damage and cracking with possibly intact external plate

physical_mechanism: Blast pressure and fragments; can damage attachments, welds, tracks, optics and thin roof/side sections; does not use AP perforation mechanics as primary outcome
projectile_parts_to_model: casing fragmentation, explosive and fuze; blast wave
material_models_needed: blast loading, fragment distribution, structural damage; a simple gameplay model may approximate only after specifying its limits
outputs: fragment impacts, blast damage, weld cracking, track/running gear effects
common_wrong_shortcut: give HE a generic armour penetration value

family: APCR/APDS or APFSDS hitting multi-layer/spaced armour
physical_mechanism: Each plate changes yaw, core damage, plugging, velocity and fragment state before next plate
projectile_parts_to_model: carry projectile state through each layer with explicit standoff; debris/jet fragments as applicable
material_models_needed: intermediate projectile state at each layer; inter-plate spacing and support/contact matter
outputs: per-layer damage, residual projectile, yaw/deflection, energy loss, downstream plate response
common_wrong_shortcut: sum thicknesses or multiply nominal penetration by a spacing bonus
